basis: Obligate neuropathy, plasma-cell disorder and common endocrinopathy; sclerotic bone lesions are major diagnostic criteria (~95%). Common skin changes omitted because of cap.
Autoimmunity, autoinflammation and immunodeficiency define the syndrome; no organ-specific damage is documented.
Primary microcephaly with intellectual disability and seizures; strabismus and external-ear malformation (microtia) each reported in 2/2 patients; small denominators.
Isolated inherited sensorineural hearing loss, documented in 17/17 patients.
Inherited retinal dysfunction with visual loss and optic disc pallor; retinal ganglion cells and optic disc belong to the ocular axis.
Hyperkeratosis confined to uterine cervical mucosa; reproductive organs have no axis.
Isolated hereditary lens dislocation; no systemic connective-tissue disease is established.
Retinal cone degeneration causes progressive visual and color-vision loss.
Cutaneous demodicosis: excessive Demodex infestation causes follicular inflammation and scaling.
Inherited melanin biosynthesis disorder defining skin and hair hypopigmentation and ocular developmental abnormalities with impaired vision.
Retinal vascular developmental disorder with exudation and detachment. Osteopenia is reported, but frequency across this subtype is insufficiently established.
Defined by developmental delay, intellectual disability and generalized epilepsy.
Fibrosis and cyst formation confined to breast parenchyma; breast has no axis.
Bipolar/major affective disorder susceptibility; purely psychiatric disease without documented organ damage.
Defining scalp folds, corneal leukoma and skeletal overgrowth/periostosis. Acromegaloid appearance alone does not establish endocrine disease.
Congenital vertebral and rib malformations. Restricted ventilation from thoracic deformity does not establish direct pulmonary damage.
Coccidioides fungal infection; pneumonia is frequent (30-79%). CNS, cutaneous and joint disease are minority manifestations; transient rashes excluded.
Histoplasma infection directly causes retinal inflammation; retinal disease belongs to the ocular axis.
Inherited oocyte maturation failure causing infertility; reproductive dysfunction without endocrine disease has no axis.
Inherited methionine catabolic defects; hepatic and neurologic damage vary by subtype, with insufficient evidence of qualifying damage across most of the umbrella.
Cerebellar hypoplasia/degeneration causes congenital ataxia and developmental impairment. Liver dysfunction is occasional (5-29%); nystagmus is neurologic.
Inherited amino-acid transport disorder defined by defective renal tubular reabsorption. Usually asymptomatic; neurologic and ocular involvement not established as common.
Histoplasma infection umbrella; pulmonary entry is typical, but qualifying lung damage in at least 30% across the group is not established. Disseminated damage is a minority.
Autoimmune encephalomyelitis in the stiff-person spectrum, commonly associated with glycine-receptor antibodies; rigidity reflects central neural dysfunction.
Persistent acquired cognitive impairment reflects brain dysfunction; dementia explicitly belongs to the neurologic axis regardless of psychiatric ancestry.
